payload.root_cause: In `truncate` (src/text.js:18-22), the truncation branch at line 21 does `return text.slice(0, max) + ellipsis;`. It slices the full `max` characters from the input and then appends the entire ellipsis, so the returned string is `max + ellipsis.length` characters long. For truncate('abcdefghij', 8): text.length (10) > max (8) and max (8) > ellipsis.length (3), so it returns 'abcdefgh' + '...' = 'abcdefgh...' (11 chars) instead of the required 8-char 'abcde...'. This violates the documented contract (docstring at line 16 and README: result length never exceeds max, ellipsis included). The slice bound must reserve room for the ellipsis, e.g. `text.slice(0, max - ellipsis.length) + ellipsis`.
evidence: src/text.js:18-22 — `function truncate(text, max, ellipsis = '...') { if (text.length <= max) return text; if (max <= ellipsis.length) return ellipsis.slice(0, max); return text.slice(0, max) + ellipsis; }` — line 21 appends the ellipsis after already taking `max` characters, producing an over-length result.
src/text.js:16 — docstring: 'Truncate text to at most `max` characters INCLUDING the ellipsis.' — the implementation contradicts this.
README.md:5 — '`truncate(text, max, ellipsis=\"...\")` — result length never exceeds `max` (ellipsis included).'

test/text.test.js:11-14 — expects truncate('abcdefghij', 8) === 'abcde...' (length 8) and truncate('abcdef', 2) === '..'; the observed actual 'abcdefgh...' (11 chars) exactly matches what line 21 computes.

payload.rationale: The truncation branch at src/text.js:21 slices the full `max` characters and then appends the ellipsis, producing a string of length `max + ellipsis.length`. Reserving room for the ellipsis by slicing to `max - ellipsis.length` makes the returned string exactly `max` characters. For truncate('abcdefghij', 8): 'abcdefghij'.slice(0, 8-3) = 'abcde', plus '...' gives 'abcde...' (8 chars), matching the documented contract and the test expectations. The other two branches (short input, and max <= ellipsis.length) already satisfy the contract and are untouched. Since we only reach this branch when max > ellipsis.length, `max - ellipsis.length` is always positive.
